collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 6-13)

collection.description: In old hearths deep in the forest, a villager and a child find a tiny clay bowl: take it home, or put it back.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Deep in the forest, under ferns taller than a person, (subject) and (friend) have found stones arranged in neat circles: old hearths, long cold. There are bits of broken pot in the soil, a worn grinding stone and, half buried by a root, a tiny clay bowl, just the right size for a child's hands.

choices.label: Put It Back Where It Was

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) wants to keep it, and (subject) agrees. They clean it gently in the stream. It's perfect, apart from a chip on the rim. (friend) puts it on the shelf in (friend.his/her) hut and doesn't use it for anything; (friend.he/she) just likes knowing it's there. Sometimes (friend.he/she) wonders who ate from it, and what they ate, and whether they liked it. (friend.He/she) thinks they probably did.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) holds the bowl for a long time. Then (friend.he/she) puts it back, exactly where it was, under the root. "It's theirs," (friend.he/she) says. (subject) doesn't argue. They walk home without saying much. Later (friend) makes a tiny clay bowl of (friend.his/her) own and fires it in the cooking fire. (friend.He/she) uses that one every day.
